small_guidance:
- Add larger tile configs to the autotune list now that small tiles compile: `(BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=16, num_warps=8, num_stages=2)` and `(BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=16, num_warps=8, num_stages=2)`. These keep SMEM well under 132 KB ((128·16+16·64)·4·2 = 24 KB) and should improve arithmetic intensity for OC=128, OUT_HW=126·126.
- Swap the program-id mapping so `pid_sp` is `program_id(0)` (the fast-varying / large dimension) and `(n, oc_tile)` is `program_id(1)`; this improves L2 reuse of the weight tile across spatial tiles within the same (n, oc).
- Fuse the post-ReLU bias add into the same epilogue (already done) but also collapse `conv.bias + self.bias` into a single precomputed bias vector at module init / forward entry, cutting one `tl.load` per tile.
large_guidance:
- Switch input layout to channels-last (NHWC) and store weights as (KH, KW, IC, OC). Then the GEMM-K axis (IC) is contiguous in memory, all `tl.load`s on x and w become fully coalesced vector loads, and the inner loop becomes a clean `tl.dot` with no gather indexing per-K-step. This is the single biggest structural win available.
- Make the K loop iterate over (kh, kw) on the outside and IC on the inside with `BLOCK_K = IC` (or 32) so the per-iteration index math (ih = oh+kh, iw = ow+kw) is hoisted out of the K loop, leaving only a contiguous IC-stride load. Currently kh/kw are recomputed every BLOCK_K=16 step from a divmod, which is expensive.
- Consider a persistent / split-N kernel: with N=128, OC=128, OUT_HW=15876, a 2D grid of (N·OC_tiles, SP_tiles) launches ~8k blocks; persistent scheduling with one program per SM iterating over a work queue improves L2 reuse of the weight tile across many spatial tiles for the same (n, oc).
